(p-٦٢٩)Surat al-Anfal (The Spoils of War)

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: the spoils belong to God and the Messenger.﴾ Al-nafl (extra gift, spoils) means booty, because it is from the bounty and gift of God. Al-anfal means the spoils of war. Disagreement arose among the Muslims concerning the spoils of Badr and their division. They asked the Messenger of God: How shall we divide them? And who has the authority over their division: the Muhajirun (the emigrants from Makkah), or the Ansar (the helpers from Madinah), or both of them together? It was said to him: Say to them: they belong to the Messenger of God, and he alone has the authority over them; he judges concerning them as he wills, and no one other than him has any judgment over them. The meaning of joining the mention of God and the Messenger is that their ruling is specific to God and His Messenger: God commands their division according to what His wisdom requires, and the Messenger carries out God's command concerning them, and the matter of their division is not left to anyone's opinion. ﴿So fear God﴾ in disputing and quarrelling, and be brothers in God. ﴿And set right what is between you﴾, meaning the state of your relations, that is, the conditions that obtain between you, until they become conditions of harmony, affection and agreement. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "dhat baynikum" is the reality of your connection, and al-bayn means connection; that is: fear God, and be united in what God and His Messenger have commanded. Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may God be pleased with him) said: It was revealed concerning us, O company of the people of Badr, when we disagreed over the spoils and our manners deteriorated because of it, so God took it out of our hands and assigned it to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he divided it among the Muslims equally. ﴿And obey God and His Messenger﴾ in what you are commanded concerning the spoils and other matters.

﴿If you are believers﴾, those whose faith is complete.

(p-٦٣٠)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, the believers are only﴾ those who are perfect in faith (al-kamilun al-iman) ﴿those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾ they are struck with fear at His mention, magnifying Him and standing in awe of His majesty, His might, and His sovereignty.

﴿And when His verses are recited to them﴾ i.e., the Qur'an.

﴿They increase them in faith﴾ they grow in certainty and tranquility through them, because the convergence of proofs is stronger for what they indicate and more firm for its footing. Or it means: they increased them in faith through those verses, because they had not believed in their rulings before.

﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾ they depend upon Him, and do not entrust their affairs to anyone other than their Lord; they fear no one and hope for nothing except Him.

Those who establish the prayer and spend out of what We have provided them.

He has combined the deeds of the heart, namely awe (wajal), sincerity (ikhlas) and reliance upon God (tawakkul), with the deeds of the limbs, namely the prayer and charity (sadaqa).

These are the true believers. This is an adjective qualifying an omitted verbal noun (masdar), meaning "These are the believers in true faith." Or it is an emphatic verbal noun (mu'akkid) for the preceding sentence, "These are the believers," as in your saying, "He is the servant of Allah, truly (haqqan)," meaning, "That is true, truly."

It is related from al-Hasan (rahimahu Allah) that a man asked him, "Are you a believer?" He said, "If you are asking me about faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, Paradise, Hell, the Resurrection, and the Reckoning, then I am a believer. But if you are asking me about His saying, ﴿Only the believers are those...﴾ [and so on], then I do not know whether I am among them or not."

It is related from al-Thawri: "Whoever claims that he is a believer in Allah truly, but does not testify that he is among the people of Paradise, has believed in only half of the verse." That is, just as he does not affirm with certainty that he is among those who receive the reward of true believers, he should not affirm with certainty that he is a true believer. Those who say, "I am a believer, God willing (in sha' Allah)," rely on this. Abu Hanifa (rahimahu Allah) did not say this. He said to Qatada, "Why do you make an exception (istithna') in your faith?" He replied, "Following Ibrahim in his saying: ﴿And the One from whom I hope He will forgive my sin on the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:82]." Abu Hanifa said to him, "Why did you not follow him in his saying: ﴿Have you not believed? He said, 'Yes, [I have believed]'﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:260]?"

It is related from Ibrahim al-Taymi: "Say, 'I am a believer truly.' If you are truthful, hold firm to it; and if you are lying, your disbelief is worse than your lie."

It is related from Ibn Abbas (radiya Allah 'anhuma) (p-631): "Whoever is not a hypocrite is a believer truly." 

Abdullah argued with Ahmad. He said, "What is your name?" He said, "Ahmad." Abdullah said, "Do you say, 'I am Ahmad truly,' or 'I am Ahmad, God willing'?" He said, "I am Ahmad truly." Abdullah said, "Since your parents named you, you do not make an exception. Yet Allah has named you a believer in the Qur'an, and you make an exception?!"

﴿For them are ranks (darajat)﴾: levels, some above others, according to the degree of their deeds.

﴿With their Lord, and forgiveness﴾: and pardon for their evil deeds. ﴿And a generous provision﴾: pure, free from the toil of earning and from fear of reckoning.

The kāf (الكاف, the prepositional particle meaning "like, as") in ﴿as your Lord brought you forth﴾ is in the accusative case (naṣb), as an adjectival clause (ṣifah) qualifying the verbal noun (maṣdar) of an implied verb. The implied sense is: "Say: the spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger," and they were established, despite their dislike, with an establishment like the bringing forth of you from your house by your Lord, while they were averse. ﴿from your house﴾ means: his house in Madinah, or Madinah itself, because it was his place of emigration and his dwelling. In its specificity to him, it is like the specificity of a house to its occupant. ﴿with truth﴾ means the bringing forth was accompanied by wisdom and rightness. ﴿And indeed a group of the believers were averse﴾ is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: He brought you forth while you were in a state of aversion. The reason was that "the caravan of Quraysh came from Syria carrying great merchandise, with forty riders, among them Abu Sufyan. Gabriel informed the Prophet (ﷺ), and he informed his companions. They liked the idea of intercepting the caravan because of the abundance of wealth and the small number of the people. When they set out, Quraysh learned of this, so Abu Jahl went out with all the people of Makkah, and he was the nafir (the summoned force), in the proverb: 'neither in the caravan nor in the nafir.' It was said to him: 'The caravan has taken the coastal road and escaped,' but he refused and marched with those with him to Badr. Badr was a water source where the Arabs would gather once a year for their market. Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended and said: 'O Muhammad, Allah has promised you one of the two groups, either the caravan or Quraysh.' The Prophet (ﷺ) consulted his companions and said: 'Which do you prefer, the caravan or the nafir?' They said: 'Rather, the caravan is more beloved to us than meeting the enemy.' The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed. He then repeated the question to them and said: 'The caravan has passed along the seashore, and this is Abu Jahl who has approached.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, take the caravan and leave the enemy.' Then Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, stood up at the Prophet's (ﷺ) anger and spoke well. Then Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah (p-632) stood up and said: 'Look to your affair and proceed. By Allah, if you were to travel to 'Adan Abyan, not a single man of the Ansar would stay behind from you.' Then al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr said: 'Proceed as Allah has commanded you, for we are with you wherever you wish. We will not say to you what the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting here﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24]. Rather: go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting along with you.' By whatever? As long as an eye among us blinks.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: 'Proceed, O Messenger of Allah, toward what you desire. By He who sent you with truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge with you, and not a single man among us would stay behind. So march with us in the blessing of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rejoiced, and Sa'd's words invigorated him. Then he said: 'Proceed in the blessing of Allah, and rejoice, for Allah has promised me one of the two groups. By Allah, it is as if I am now looking at the places where the people will fall.'" The aversion of some of them was due to His saying ﴿And indeed a group of the believers were averse﴾. Shaykh Abu Mansur, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is possible that they were hypocrites who disliked that out of conviction. It is possible that they were sincere, and that their dislike was a dislike of natural disposition, because they were not prepared for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 6:

﴿They argue with you concerning the truth﴾ The truth about which they argued with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the going out to meet the armed host (al-nafir) rather than the caravan (al-'ir), because of their preference for it over the caravan. ﴿After it had become clear﴾ after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had informed them that they would be given victory. Their argument was their saying: "We did not go out except for the caravan. Why did you not say to us, 'Let us prepare'?" This was due to their dislike of fighting.

﴿As if they were being driven toward death while they were looking on﴾ He likened their condition, in the extremity of their fear, while they were being led toward victory and booty, to the condition of one who is dragged to be killed and driven in humiliation toward death, while he is witnessing its causes, looking at them, and having no doubt about them. It was said: their fear was due to the small number (of their force), and that they were infantry, and there were only two horsemen among them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 7:

﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. "Idh" (when) is in the accusative, governed by "udhkur" (remember). "Ihda" (one of) is the second object (maf'ul thani). ﴿That it would be yours﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿one of the two groups﴾, and the two groups are: the caravan (al-'ir) and the army (al-nafir). The estimated meaning is: "And when Allah promised you that one of the two groups would be yours." ﴿And you wished that the one without thorn (shawka) would be yours﴾, that is, the caravan. "Dhat al-shawka" means "the one possessing weapons," and shawka was with the army because of their number and equipment. That is, you wished that the caravan would be yours, because it was the group that had no weapons, and you did not want the other group. ﴿And Allah wished to establish the truth﴾, that is, to confirm it and elevate it.

﴿By His words﴾, by His revealed verses concerning the fighting of the one possessing thorn, and by what He commanded the angels of descending to give support, and by what He decreed of their killing and their being thrown into the well of Badr.

﴿And to cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers﴾. "Dabir" means the last, the end. It is the subject (fa'il), from "dabara," meaning when one turns his back. Cutting off the dabir is an expression for total eradication (istie'sal). The meaning is: you desire immediate gain and lowly affairs, while Allah, exalted is He, desires lofty affairs, the support of truth, and the elevation of the word. How far apart are the two aims! For this reason He chose for you the group possessing thorn, broke their strength through your weakness, and made you mighty and them abased.

Li-yuḥiqqa al-ḥaqqa (so that He might establish the truth) is connected with yaqṭaʿa (cut off), or with an omitted element whose estimated form is: li-yuḥiqqa al-ḥaqqa. "And to nullify falsehood" (wa-yubṭila al-bāṭila) — He did that. The omitted element is placed later (in the sense of being deferred) in order to convey restriction (al-ikhtiṣāṣ), i.e., He did not do it except for these two purposes: the establishing and manifesting of Islam, and the nullifying and annihilating of disbelief (al-kufr). This is not a repetition, because the first (statement) distinguishes between the two intentions, while this one explains His purpose in what He did, namely choosing the party with the might (dhāt al-shawka) over the other for them (the believers), and granting them victory over it. "Even though the criminals disliked it" — the criminals (al-mujrimūn) being the polytheists (al-mushrikūn) — disliked that.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 9:

﴿When you sought help from your Lord﴾ is either a substitution (badal) for "when He promised you" or it is connected to His saying: ﴿so that He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood﴾. Their seeking help (istighatha) was that when they knew that fighting was unavoidable, they began calling upon God, saying: "O our Lord, help us against Your enemy; O Helper of those who seek help, aid us." It is a request for ghawth (relief), which is deliverance from something disliked.

﴿So He answered you﴾: fa-ajaba (He responded). The original form of ﴿that I will reinforce you﴾ is bi-anni mumiddukum; the preposition was dropped, and the verb istajaba was made to govern it directly, so that its place became accusative: ﴿with a thousand of the angels, following one another﴾. The reading (murdifin) with a fatha is that of Medina; others read it with a kasra on the dal. The kasra means that they caused others to follow them (ardafu ghayrahum), while the fatha means that each angel made another angel follow him. It is said: radifahu, when he followed him; and ardaftuhu iyyahu, when you made him follow it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 10:

﴿And Allah did not make it﴾, that is, the reinforcement that was indicated by ﴿your reinforcement﴾, ﴿except as good news﴾, except as a glad tiding to you of victory, ﴿and that your hearts might be reassured thereby﴾. That is to say: you sought help and humbled yourselves before Allah because of your small numbers, so the reinforcement with the angels was a glad tiding to you of victory, and a calming for you, and a strengthening of your hearts. ﴿And victory is not from anywhere but from Allah﴾, that is: do not reckon that victory comes from the angels, for the true Helper is Allah, to you and to the angels. Or, ﴿and victory is not﴾ from the angels or others among the means ﴿except from Allah﴾, and the one who is victorious is the one whom Allah has helped.

There is disagreement concerning the fighting of the angels on the day of Badr. It is said: Jibril, peace be upon him, descended with five hundred angels upon the right wing, and with him was Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and Mika'il with five hundred upon the left wing, and with them was ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, in the form of men wearing white garments and white turbans, whose tails they had let hang down between their shoulders. Then they fought, until Abu Jahl said to Ibn Mas'ud: "From where were the blows coming to us while we did not see the figure?" He said: "From the direction of the angels." He said: "Then they overcame us, not you." It is also said: they did not fight; they only increased the number of the force and strengthened the believers. Otherwise, one angel is sufficient to destroy the people of the world.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾ in granting victory to His allies, ﴿Wise﴾ in subduing His enemies.

﴿When He covers you with drowsiness﴾ is a second substitute (*badal*) for ﴿when He promised you﴾. Or it is in the accusative (*mansub*) governed by ﴿the help﴾, or by an implied ﴿remember﴾.

(*yughshikum*) is the reading of Madani (the reader from Madina).

﴿drowsiness﴾ means sleep. On both readings the subject is God: (*yaghshakumu al-nu'as*) is the reading of Makki and Abu 'Amr.

﴿security﴾ is an object of purpose (*maf'ul lahu*), meaning: when you slumber for security, that is, for your safety. Or it is a verbal noun (*masdar*), meaning: you were made secure with security. Sleep removes fear and refreshes the soul. ﴿from Him﴾ is a qualifier of it, meaning: a security coming to you from God.

(*wa-yunzilu*) with light stress is the reading of Makki and Basri; with heavy stress it is the reading of the others. ﴿upon you from the sky﴾ ﴿water﴾ means rain, ﴿to purify you thereby﴾ with the water from ritual impurity (*hadath*) and major impurity (*janabah*).

﴿and to remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾ means his whispering to them and his frightening them with thirst. Or it means major impurity from wet dreams, because it comes from Satan, who had whispered to them that there is no victory with major impurity.

﴿and to strengthen your hearts﴾ with patience, ﴿and to make firm the feet thereby﴾: that is, with the water, since the feet were sinking in the sand. Or it means with the strengthening, because when patience settles in the heart it makes the foot firm in the places of battle.

**Surah 8, verse 12, from al-Nasafi's commentary (Madarik al-Tanzil):**

﴿When﴾ is a third substitute (badal) for ﴿when He promised you﴾, or it is in the accusative governed by "yuthabbita" (He may strengthen). ﴿Your Lord revealed to the angels: "Surely I am with you"﴾ in support, ﴿so strengthen those who believe﴾ with good tidings. The angel would walk in front of the ranks in the form of a man and say: "Rejoice, for surely Allah is your helper." ﴿I shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve﴾: it is the filling of the heart with fear. And "al-ru'ub" (the terror) is read by Shami and Ali.

﴿Then strike﴾ is a command to the believers, or to the angels, and in it is evidence that they fought. ﴿Above the necks﴾, that is, the upper parts of the necks, which are the places of slaughter, to make the heads fly off; or it means the heads, since they are above the necks, that is, striking the skulls. ﴿And strike from them every fingertip﴾: it is the fingers, and he means the extremities. The meaning is: strike the vital spots and the extremities, because a blow either lands on a vital spot or on a non-vital spot, so He commanded them to combine both kinds against them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 13–14:

﴿That﴾ refers to what befell them of striking, killing, and immediate punishment. It is a mubtada' (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿because they opposed Allah and His Messenger﴾. That is, that punishment befell them because of their mushaqqah (opposition), i.e., their contrariety. It is derived from al-shaqq (splitting), because each of two adversaries is in a split opposite to the split of the other. Likewise al-mu'adah (enmity) and al-mukhasamah (contention), because this one is in one 'adwah (side) and khasm (direction), i.e., side, and that one is in another 'adwah and khasm. ﴿And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ The kaf in "dhalika" is for addressing the Messenger, or for every addressee. In "dhalikum" it is for the disbelievers, in the manner of iltifat (shift of grammatical person). Its place in i'rab is raf' (nominative), as "dhalikum" with "al-'iqab" (the punishment) as the predicate, or "al-'iqab" as the subject.

﴿That, so taste it﴾. The waw in ﴿and that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire﴾ is in the meaning of ma'a (with). That is: taste this immediate punishment together with the deferred one that is theirs in the Hereafter. The apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun.
